title: Sale Ad Creatives With Editable Offers | AIVideosUGC
description: Build a sale ad from one product photo. Type the confirmed price, code, and end date in the editor, then reuse the same scene when the offer changes.
lead: Sale ad creatives are the pictures and videos for your sale. Paste a product link and get a script, an actor, and a spoken voice, before the price and the code are final.

faq.q: Will the discount be printed on the image for me?
faq.a: The product link can bring in the item details. You still confirm the percent, the price, the code, and the end date in the editor, so you can check every character.

faq.q: Can I reuse the scene for the next promotion?
faq.a: Yes. The product scene is separate from the offer. Replace the text, the spoken voice, or the timer when the sale changes, and keep the same picture.

faq.q: Can I show the old price next to the sale price?
faq.a: Only if you really charged that old price. Before you publish it, check the rules where you sell for an old price next to the new one.

faq.q: Can I change the timer on the sale video?
faq.a: Yes. Set the end time in the editor and move it if the end date changes. You choose when the countdown stops.

faq.q: How many credits does a sale photo or video use?
faq.a: Credits are what each photo or video uses. A photo uses 24 credits. A video uses 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, or 120 for 30. You see the cost before you start. If it fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Can the sale ad use an actor from the library?
faq.a: Yes. Pick one, describe a look, or build one from a short clip of you. If a person appears, that person is generated, not a real customer or a celebrity.

faq.q: Can I publish the file as a paid sale ad?
faq.a: Yes. Publish in one click to TikTok, Instagram, or Meta, or download it. Meta here means Facebook and Instagram. The download has no AIVideosUGC watermark. Each app still has its own ad rules.

faq.q: Can I make sale ads for many products at once?
faq.a: Yes. You can run many product links at once, and each one comes back as its own ad. Check every file before it is published.

faq.q: Can the ad start from a product link?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the product page. The photos and the details come in, ready for the ad. You can also upload one product photo.

faq.q: Can my own tools request sale ads?
faq.a: Yes. An API is a connection that lets your own tools ask for a sale ad from a product link. The file stays in your account until you share it.

faq.q: Can I add a spoken voice, music, and captions?
faq.a: Yes. Choose an AI voice, a track from the music library, and captions (the words on screen). The same script can be spoken in another language.

faq.q: What shape should the sale video use?
faq.a: A product photo is square. A clip from the same photo runs 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Pick a shape: tall 9:16 for a phone, square 1:1, wide 16:9, or 4:3 and 3:4. Each video is a separate run.

faq.q: How much empty space should I leave for the offer?
faq.a: Leave clear room for the offer line and the code without covering the product. Check the smallest screen you will use and make sure both stay readable.

reviews.h2: How shops make a sale banner for an online store
reviews.lead: Three ways a shop leaves room for an offer that is not final yet.

items.t: Leave open space beside the jar
items.d: They paste the product link and ask for a clean counter with empty room on one side. The percent off is typed later, so a changed number does not need a new scene.

items.t: Run the jacket scene again next week
items.d: They keep the same jacket scene and swap the actor's line for the next code. Only the offer text in the editor changes.

items.t: Fold the blanket, then set the timer
items.d: They show the blanket in use and set the end time in the editor once the sale window is real.
